The Fountain of Life Church has faulted the issuance of a bench warrant against its Senior Pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, claiming he was not served with the restraining order against him and that pending applications challenging the court’s orders were not determined before the warrant was issued. The church also questioned why the matter was heard despite not appearing on the court’s case list. It claimed that journalists were asked to leave the courtroom before the warrant was issued and noted that the presiding judge subsequently recused herself. In a statement issued on Thursday and made available to our correspondents, the church expressed “grave concern” over the proceedings before Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin of the Lagos State High Court, which resulted in the issuance of the bench warrant. It said its legal representatives maintained that Odukoya had not been duly served with the restraining order, originating processes and accompanying documents, either personally or by substituted means, as directed by the court. “It is important to clarify that, according to his legal representatives, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has, to date, not been duly served with the restraining order together with the originating processes and accompanying documents, either personally or by substituted means, in accordance with the express directives of the court itself,” the statement said. The church’s lawyers also identified five issues they considered significant concerns in the proceedings. First, the church said the court’s directives on the service of the originating processes and accompanying documents, contained in its orders of November 18 and 23, remained unfulfilled. Third, the church said the matter was not on the court’s case list for Thursday. Fourth, it claimed members of the media were directed to leave the courtroom before the bench warrant was issued. Fifth, it faulted the decision to issue the warrant before determining the pending applications, adding that the presiding judge recused herself afterwards. “The bench warrant was issued without first determining the outstanding applications, following which the presiding judge recused herself,” the statement said. The church noted that the developments took place within eight days of the initial ex parte order and before December 1, the date originally fixed by the court for mention of the matter. It said the circumstances raised “serious questions regarding due process, fair hearing and the administration of justice”. The church further disclosed that its legal representatives were actively challenging the orders, their enforceability and the procedural and jurisdictional issues arising from the proceedings before the appropriate courts, including the Court of Appeal. Clarifying the implication of the bench warrant, it said, “For clarity, the issuance of a bench warrant does not constitute a conviction or a final determination of the substantive leadership dispute.” On the leadership question, the church maintained that Odukoya remained its duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees. “The Church maintains its position, based on the advice of its legal representatives, that Pastor Jimmy Odukoya remains its duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees. This position forms part of the matters being pursued through the judicial process,” it said. The church reaffirmed its commitment to the rule of law, constitutional governance and the pursuit of justice, saying it would exhaust all available legal remedies within the Nigerian judicial system. It also appealed to its members, friends and the general public to remain calm, united, prayerful and steadfast, adding that its commitment to the church’s spiritual mandate, founding principles and vision remained unchanged. The statement followed Thursday’s proceedings at the Lagos State High Court in Ikoyi, where Justice Adewunmi-Oshin issued a bench warrant against Odukoya after he failed to appear in court in a contempt case instituted by the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church. The warrant followed an earlier order made on November 18 restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head or interfering with its governance and activities. The leadership crisis became public on November 17 when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that it no longer recognised Odukoya as senior pastor. The trustees cited the church’s constitution, and a video said to contain succession instructions from its late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya. They subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader. Odukoya rejected his removal and filed a separate suit at the Federal High Court in Lagos challenging the trustees’ decision. He had also previously said he was aware of the restraining order but had not been formally served with the court documents. Christabel Ndoeche
